title: Getting Started
summary: Turn Kneady on, find an object's regions, bend an arm by dragging it, and undo.

steps.title: Turn Kneady on
text: Kneady lets you pose and shape a model by dragging the model itself. It starts out off in every file.
Turn it on with the Kneady button in the 3D view's header, or at the top of the sidebar's Kneady tab. It is lit for you there now.

steps.title: Find the regions
text: Move the mouse over the arm. With Kneady on, hovering an object shows its regions, each in its own color: here the forearm and the upper arm.
The region under the mouse brightens and shows its buttons. Move from one to the other and the hover follows.

steps.title: Bend the elbow
text: Press on the forearm and drag up: the elbow bends. Drag down to bend it back, and left or right to swing it.
Let go to keep the pose. Nothing needs selecting first - a drag goes to the region you pressed on. A click without a drag still selects, as it always has.

steps.title: Undo it
text: Press Ctrl+Z. A drag is one step of undo, like any other edit in Blender, and the elbow goes back to where it was.

steps.title: How much Kneady says
text: Help, beside the Kneady button in the sidebar, sets how much Kneady tells you as you work. Learn shows every key a button takes, Inform what each drag does, and Quiet only the names.
Help is yours, not the file's: it stays the same in every file you open.
That's the start. Press Finish to go back to your own file.
